Set trip maximum speed

Source: R/set_max_speed.R
set_max_speed.Rd

Caps the speed of the specified trips: each part of a trip that is faster than max_speed is slowed down to max_speed, by changing the arrival_time and departure_time columns in stop_times. Parts of the trips that are already slower are left unchanged.

Usage

set_max_speed(
  gtfs,
  max_speed,
  route_id = NULL,
  trip_id = NULL,
  unit = "km/h",
  first_stop = NULL,
  last_stop = NULL,
  from = NULL,
  to = NULL,
  route_type = NULL
)

Arguments

gtfs

A GTFS object, as created by read_gtfs().

max_speed

A number. The maximum speed allowed, in the unit given by unit.

route_id

A character vector including the route_ids whose trips have their speeds capped. If route_id, trip_id and route_type are all NULL (the default), the speeds of every trip in the GTFS are capped. route_ids not listed in trips are ignored, with a warning.

trip_id

A character vector including the trip_ids to have their speeds capped. When given together with route_id, the trips of both are capped.

unit

A string representing the unit in which the speed is given. One of "km/h" (the default), "m/s" or "mph" (miles per hour).

first_stop

A string. The stop_id where the segment whose speeds are capped starts. If NULL (the default), the segment starts at each trip's first stop.

last_stop

A string. The stop_id where the segment ends. If NULL (the default), the segment ends at each trip's last stop.

from

A string, in the "HH:MM:SS" format. Only trips that depart from the segment's first stop at or after from are changed. If NULL (the default), there is no lower limit.

to

A string, in the "HH:MM:SS" format. Only trips that depart from the segment's first stop at or before to are changed. If NULL (the default), there is no upper limit.

route_type

An integer vector of route_types (see filter_by_route_type()). If given, only trips of routes of these types are changed; together with the other selection arguments, it restricts their selection. route_types not listed in routes are ignored. If NULL (the default), trips of any type are changed.

Value

A GTFS object with the time columns of its stop_times adjusted.

Details

The speed of each span between two consecutive stops with times is its length, as calculated by get_trip_length() along the trip's shape (or as straight lines between stops, with a warning, if there are no shapes), divided by the time between the departure from the first stop and the arrival at the second. Stops with blank times inside a span are kept blank. The stops table is required. Spans whose length is NA (e.g. in trips not linked to a shape) are left unchanged.

Each span faster than max_speed has its duration increased to its length divided by max_speed, rounded up to the next second, so new times may include seconds even if the original times were given in whole minutes. Spans with zero duration are treated the same way. All the later times of the trip are shifted by the accumulated extra time, so dwell times are kept. Spans whose arrival is earlier than the previous departure are left unchanged, with a warning. This usually happens when times after midnight are written as "00:30:00" instead of "24:30:00". Only stop_times is modified.

With first_stop and last_stop, only the spans between them are capped. first_stop is matched at its first visit in stop_sequence order, and last_stop at its next visit after that (which may be the same stop), as in set_trip_speed(). Times before first_stop don't change, and the times at and after last_stop are shifted by the extra time. The given stops must have a time, so that no span crosses them. If only last_stop is given, the trip's first stop doesn't need one, because spans start at stops with times. Trips that don't visit first_stop and then last_stop, or that have blank times there, are left unchanged, with a warning if they were given in trip_id or route_id (not if they were selected only by route_type). from and to are compared with the departure at the segment's first stop (or its arrival, if the departure is blank) as written in stop_times, so use times past "24:00:00" for departures after midnight. For trips listed in frequencies, these are template times, not actual departures. Trips without a time there are left unchanged.

See also

set_trip_speed(), get_trip_speed()

Examples

data_path <- system.file("extdata/spo_gtfs.zip", package = "gtfstools")

gtfs <- read_gtfs(data_path)

# the trip is faster than 30 km/h between some of its stops
get_trip_speed(gtfs, "CPTM L07-0", by = "segment")
#>     route_id    trip_id segment from_stop_id to_stop_id    speed
#>       <char>     <char>   <int>       <char>     <char>    <num>
#>  1: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0       1        18940      18920 26.60738
#>  2: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0       2        18920      18919 18.18377
#>  3: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0       3        18919      18917 11.93590
#>  4: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0       4        18917      18916 15.07881
#>  5: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0       5        18916      18965 16.28882
#>  6: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0       6        18965      18923 21.31043
#>  7: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0       7        18923      18922 15.08821
#>  8: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0       8        18922    4114459 17.68714
#>  9: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0       9      4114459      18921 31.53864
#> 10: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0      10        18921      18924 32.98105
#> 11: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0      11        18924      18925 36.47943
#> 12: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0      12        18925      18926 20.48514
#> 13: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0      13        18926      18971 26.54381
#> 14: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0      14        18971      18972 52.84955
#> 15: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0      15        18972      18973 28.27469
#> 16: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0      16        18973      18974 44.78676
#> 17: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0      17        18974      18975 38.29072

gtfs_capped <- set_max_speed(gtfs, max_speed = 30, trip_id = "CPTM L07-0")
get_trip_speed(gtfs_capped, "CPTM L07-0", by = "segment")
#>     route_id    trip_id segment from_stop_id to_stop_id    speed
#>       <char>     <char>   <int>       <char>     <char>    <num>
#>  1: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0       1        18940      18920 26.60738

#>  3: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0       3        18919      18917 11.93590
#>  4: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0       4        18917      18916 15.07881
#>  5: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0       5        18916      18965 16.28882
#>  6: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0       6        18965      18923 21.31043
#>  7: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0       7        18923      18922 15.08821
#>  8: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0       8        18922    4114459 17.68714
#>  9: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0       9      4114459      18921 29.97732
#> 10: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0      10        18921      18924 29.98277
#> 11: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0      11        18924      18925 29.98309
#> 12: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0      12        18925      18926 20.48514
#> 13: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0      13        18926      18971 26.54381
#> 14: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0      14        18971      18972 29.98556
#> 15: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0      15        18972      18973 28.27469

#> 17: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0      17        18974      18975 29.98295

# the later stops are shifted, so the trip ends later
 get_start_and_end_times(gtfs, trip_id = "CPTM L07-0")
#> start_time   end_time 
#> "04:00:00" "06:16:00" 
 get_start_and_end_times(gtfs_capped, trip_id = "CPTM L07-0")
#> start_time   end_time 
#> "04:00:00" "06:31:13" 

# cap the speed only between two stops. the spans before and after them
# are not capped
gtfs_capped <- set_max_speed(
  gtfs,
  max_speed = 30,
  trip_id = "CPTM L07-0",
  first_stop = "18921",
  last_stop = "18974"
)
get_trip_speed(gtfs_capped, "CPTM L07-0", by = "segment")
#>     route_id    trip_id segment from_stop_id to_stop_id    speed

# cap the speed of all the trips of all routes of the GTFS feed
gtfs_capped <- set_max_speed(gtfs, max_speed = 8)
